question: Is the installed postcss-selector-parser@6.1.5 genuinely patched for GHSA-rj75-hqrm-r3gf?

officialAdvisory.summary: PostCSS: Quadratic complexity in flat selector parsing allows CPU exhaustion
officialAdvisory.osvRecord: github/advisory-database advisories/github-reviewed/2026/10/GHSA-rj75-hqrm-r3gf: one range {introduced 0, fixed 7.1.6}; single commit e65fe52e94 (2026-10-05) — never updated
officialAdvisory.reachabilityStatement: Only consumers that parse untrusted, attacker-supplied selectors synchronously in a request path are exposed ... Ordinary build-time use on trusted sources is not affected.

release_6.1.5.notes: fix ... (CVE-2026-104844 / GHSA-rj75-hqrm-r3gf) backported from 7.1.6 (#346). 6.1.5 is the patched version for the 6.x line. Published under the legacy-v6 dist-tag.

upstream.codeComparison: Style-normalised (quotes, whitespace, comments) added/removed code lines of src/parser.js: 12 in each commit, IDENTICAL. Covers all three passes named by the advisory: uniqs() (Set), the Sass-interpolation filter (Set), and the indices.forEach membership tests (classIndexes / idIndexes Sets).

proofOfConcept.method: Upstream's own regression test (src/__tests__/complexity.mjs @ 6.1.5): ratio = fastest-of-3 time(atom.repeat(60000)) / time(`${atom} `.repeat(60000)); healthy < 2 (linear ≈ < 1); quadratic builds measured 4–8 upstream. Atoms: '.a' (classes), '#a' (ids), '#{a}' (Sass interpolations). Plus upstream's correctness assertions.

headline400KB.payload: '.a'.repeat(200000) — 400,000 bytes, 200,000 class nodes (the advisory's '400 KB ... ~34 s' case)

advisoryCorrection.pending: github/advisory-database#10456 (open, 2026-10-20) by the package maintainer @MoOx: ranges -> {introduced 0, fixed 6.1.5} and {introduced 7.0.0, fixed 7.1.6}
advisoryCorrection.note: #10457 (open), #10481 and #10676 are duplicates of #10456. #10481 and #10676 were closed by their own authors (closed_by = author) after the maintainer asked them to close; neither was rejected by GitHub.

conclusion: Genuinely patched in code and behaviour (identical fix to 7.1.6, verified artifact, PoC fixed). The official advisory still lists 6.1.5 as affected because its range predates the 6.1.5 release; npm audit will keep reporting it until GitHub applies #10456. Roducq's use is build-time on trusted sources, which the advisory itself states is not affected.
